title: Settings
name: Name
emailVerifyPending: We sent a confirmation link to {email}. Your email changes once you confirm it there.
emailChangeNoMail: A confirmation link is sent by email to confirm a new address, which this hub can't deliver yet — your email won't change until email is set up.
uiModeDesc: Choose how much of Tugra you see. Switch any time.
uiModeFleetDesc: Full control plane: servers, teams, deploys, monitoring.
uiModeHomeDesc: Simple launcher for your apps — the extras stay out of the way.
sessionsDesc: Sign out of every device, including this one. You'll need to sign in again.
logoutEverywhereConfirm: Sign out of all devices? Every session (including this one) will be ended and you'll need to sign in again.
passwordMin: New password must be at least 8 characters.
recoveryCodesDesc: Save these somewhere safe. Each code works once if you lose your authenticator. They won't be shown again.
sudoDesc: Confirm with your password and a current 2FA code (from your authenticator, or a recovery code).
channelsDesc: Deploy, server and SSL alerts over email, Slack, Discord and more.
apiTokensDesc: Personal access tokens for the API/CLI. Use as a Bearer token.
tokenOnce: Copy this token now — it won't be shown again.
noTokens: Create a token to use the REST API or CLI.
tokenScopesHint: Every token can read. Grant only what this token needs.
scopeReadSecretsDesc: Reveal env vars, credentials, and other secrets.
apiAccessDesc: Control token (API/CLI) access to this instance. Your browser session is never affected.
apiEnabledHint: When off, all personal access tokens are rejected — the web app keeps working.
apiAllowedIpsHint: One IP or CIDR range per line. Leave empty to allow any address. Requires a trusted reverse proxy to be accurate behind one.
licenseDesc: Activate a signed license to unlock the Pro or Cloud edition. Buy one from Tugra, then paste the license token below — no restart needed.
licenseTokenHint: The signed token you received after purchase. Leave the field empty and press Remove to downgrade.
licenseNotVerified: The license was stored but did not verify
ssoDesc: Let your team sign in with your OIDC identity provider (Okta, Entra ID, Keycloak, Auth0, …). Accounts are created automatically on first sign-in.
ssoEnabledHint: When on, the login page offers an “Sign in with SSO” button. Requires an issuer, client ID and client secret.
ssoAllowedDomainsHint: One domain per line (e.g. company.com). New users may sign in only from these domains. Leave empty to allow any domain the provider authenticates.
updatesDesc: Track new Tugra releases and choose how they're applied.
updateOwnerApplies: The instance owner applies updates from Settings.
updaterBehindNote: The update helper runs {version}, older than this hub. The hub brings it forward by itself once it can reach this machine's agent and no update is running; nothing for you to do.
updaterRefreshingNote: The update helper is being refreshed to match this hub. It restarts in a few seconds.
updaterFailedNote: The update helper still runs {version} and the automatic refresh did not finish. Updates keep working, but run scripts/install.sh on the server once to bring it (and the scripts next to it) up to date.
updateAuto: Apply updates automatically (patch releases, and the next beta on a beta build)
updateAutoHint: Patch releases — and the next beta while you run a beta — are applied automatically. New minor/major versions and the move from beta to stable always wait for you.
channelAutoHint: Automatic follows the running build: a beta build tracks Beta, a release build tracks Stable. Pin a channel to override.
updateChecksDisabled: Update checks are turned off for this deployment (TUGRA_UPDATE_CHECKS=0).
updateChecksEvery: Checks run every {minutes} minutes and whenever the panel is opened.
updateFailed: The update failed. Check the server logs and try again.
updateTimedOut: The update did not complete: the new version never came up. Check the update helper's log on the server (docker logs tugra-updater), then try again.
updateDiskShort: Not enough free disk space. The update needs about {need} free on {path}, but only {have} is available. Free some space (remove unused Docker images or volumes and old backups, or enlarge the disk), then click Update now again. Nothing was changed.
updateDiskFull: The disk filled up while pulling the images. Free some space (remove unused Docker images or volumes and old backups, or enlarge the disk), then click Update now again. Nothing was changed.
updateHalfTitle: An earlier update did not finish
updateHalfNote: This server's configuration already names {envVersion}, but it is still running {runningVersion}: an earlier update stopped half-way (for example because the disk was full). Nothing is broken. Finish update pulls what is missing and completes it; if {envVersion} cannot be pulled, the configuration is put back to {runningVersion}.
updateHalfNoRelease: This server's configuration already names {envVersion}, but it is still running {runningVersion}: an earlier update stopped half-way, and no newer release is published to finish it with. Set TUGRA_VERSION={runningVersion} in the server's .env to put it back.
updateRecoveryRequired: The update failed and the previous version could not be fully restored — the instance may be partly updated. Recover manually: set TUGRA_VERSION to the previous version in .env and recreate hub-api + web (the server logs print the exact command).
updateInProgress: An update is already in progress.
updateUnconfigured: Automatic updates aren't configured on this instance.
updateNotifyOnly: This is a minor/major release — review the changelog, then use your installer to upgrade.
updateNeedsIntermediate: This release can't be skipped to directly — upgrade to an intermediate version first.
telemetryDesc: Share anonymous stats — aggregate counts (servers, apps, databases, deploys, and the like) plus your Tugra version, edition and OS — so we can see what to build next. The payload carries no IP, hostname, domain, email, app or server name; it is keyed by a random, stable id, and the receiver does not store your IP. You can turn this off anytime.
telemetryEnabledHint: Helps steer Tugra's development. Aggregate counts + version/edition/OS under a random, stable id — never names or secrets.
telemetryForcedOff: Telemetry is turned off by the server environment (TUGRA_TELEMETRY=0). Remove that variable to let this toggle take effect.
telemetrySendError: Couldn't reach the stats endpoint (that's fine — it'll retry later)
telemetryResetDone: A fresh anonymous ID was generated
telemetryThanks: Thanks — you're helping Tugra get better
sectionInstanceHint: Instance-wide settings — visible to the instance owner only.
brandingDesc: Replace the Tugra name, logo, favicon and accent color with your own, and hide the "Powered by Tugra" footer. Applies across the panel and the login page.
brandingProHint: White-label is a Pro feature. Activate a license under Plan & license to brand this instance.
brandingHidePoweredHint: Removes the Tugra attribution from the login page footer.
mail_desc: How this panel sends password-reset, verification and invite emails. Configure it here instead of editing MAIL_* environment variables.
mail_effectiveEnv: Sending through the MAIL_* environment variables (no provider selected here).
mail_effectiveNone: Email is not configured — links are written to the hub log and nothing is sent.
mail_fromHint: e.g. Tugra <no-reply@example.com>. Must be a verified sender at your provider.
mail_resendHint: Resend is sent over its SMTP relay (smtp.resend.com). Only the API key and a from address are needed.
mail_testFailedGeneric: Test email could not be sent
mail_testNeedsSave: Save your changes first — the test uses the saved settings.
hubBackup_desc: Scheduled backup of Tugra's own database (your apps, servers, settings and encrypted secrets). Runs on the local agent and is always encrypted.
hubBackup_saveFailed: Could not save the backup settings
hubBackup_envWarning: Your .env (SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY) is NOT included in this backup. Keep it offsite — without it the backup cannot be decrypted. Destination encryption keys are inside this backup, protected by your .env key.
hubBackup_localWarning: Stored on this same disk. Choose an S3 destination for real disaster recovery.
hubBackup_alwaysEncrypted: Always encrypted with a key derived from your .env — this cannot be turned off.
keysExport_minLength: The passphrase must be at least 12 characters.
keysExport_warning: The file holds the decryption key of every encrypted backup destination. Treat it like your .env: keep it offline, never email it.
keysExport_done: Downloaded {name} ({count} destination key(s)). Open it with: openssl enc -d -aes-256-cbc -pbkdf2 -iter 600000 -md sha256 -in <file>
keysExport_undecryptable: {count} destination key(s) could not be read and are missing from the file: {ids}
panelTlsDesc: Automatic TLS for this control panel. The domain is set at install (--domain --auto-tls); here you can check it and re-apply if the certificate or router needs re-provisioning.
panelTlsOff: Not configured. Run the installer with --domain and --auto-tls to turn on automatic HTTPS for the panel.
panelTlsOriginMismatch: The panel domain does not match this instance's public URL — HTTPS will not work until they match (re-run the installer with the right --domain).
panelTlsEmailBad: No valid Let's Encrypt email is set, so the certificate can't be issued. Re-run the installer with --acme-email.
secretsKeyDesc: Stored secrets are encrypted with data keys that are themselves protected by SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY. Rotate the active key here without restarting; old keys stay readable until nothing uses them.
secretsKeyTotals: {current} secrets under the current key · {stale} still on an old key · {unreadable} unreadable
secretsKeyUnreadableHint: Unreadable secrets were written with a key that is no longer configured. Add that key to SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS and re-encrypt, or re-enter those values.
secretsKeyRecoveryCodes: {count} two-factor recovery codes were issued before the rotation. They keep working while the previous key is configured; users should regenerate them before it is removed.
secretsKeyRemovable: Every stored secret is under the current key — you can remove SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS from the environment and restart.
secretsKeyPending: Some secrets are still under a previous key. Keep SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS set until this card says it is safe to remove.
secretsKeyLastRun: Last run {when}: {rewritten} rewritten · {alreadyCurrent} already current · {unreadable} unreadable · {skipped} skipped · {errors} errors
secretsKeyBackupNote: Hub backups carry their wrapped data keys, so restoring one needs only the SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY that was set when it was taken. Hub backup encryption itself still uses a passphrase derived from that .env key, so keep the old .env key somewhere safe until you no longer need to restore older backups. Rotating the data key does not change SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY.
secretsKeyRotateBody: A new random key becomes the active key right now, with no restart and no change to your .env file. Existing secrets stay readable under their old keys.
secretsKeyRotateStale: The active key changed while this page was open. The list was refreshed; check it and try again.

secretsKeyErr.referenced: Stored secrets still use this key. Re-encrypt first.
secretsKeyErr.grace: This key was replaced moments ago. Wait a minute, then retire it.
secretsKeyErr.rotation_running: A re-encryption is running. Wait for it to finish.
secretsKeyErr.ring_degraded: A data key cannot be unwrapped with the configured .env key, so changes are blocked.
secretsKeyErr.no_root: No configured .env key can unwrap this key. Put the old key back in SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS.
secretsKeyErr.not_decrypt_only: Only a decrypt-only key can be retired.
secretsKeyErr.not_retired: Only a retired key can be restored.
secretsKeyErr.already_env_root: The .env key is already the encryption key.
secretsKeyErr.stale_current: The active key changed. Reload and try again.
secretsKeyErr.unknown_key: That key is not managed here.

secretsKeyBlocked.grace: Replaced moments ago, wait a minute

secretsKeyDegraded: The key ring is degraded: {reason}. Fix SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY (or put the previous key in SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS) and restart. Rotation and retiring are disabled meanwhile.
secretsKeyDowngradeNote: Some secrets are stored under a rotated key. Before rolling back to an older Tugra release, switch back to the .env key and let the re-encryption finish.
secretsKeyBackToEnvConfirm: Make the SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY from your .env the encryption key again and re-encrypt all secrets under it? Rotated keys stay readable until you retire them.
appearanceDesc: How Tugra looks on this device. Stored in your browser only — nothing is sent to the server.
appearanceThemeHint: Light, dark, follow your system, or build your own.
appearanceScaleHint: Make everything a little smaller to fit more on screen. Phones always use 100%.
appearanceWidthHint: Let pages use the full window, or keep them in a centered column on wide screens.
appearanceNavHint: The sidebar either runs edge to edge or floats as a framed panel on a dotted background.
appearanceStyleHint: Flat is the standard look. 3D gives cards a raised edge that lifts on hover.
appearanceChartTimesHint: Chart tooltips and deployment timestamps show your local time, optionally with the same moment in UTC.
tokenRotateBody: A new secret is issued for "{name}" and the current one stops working immediately. Update every script or CI job that uses it.
updateReloadHint: This page is still running the old version until you reload.
